overrides_applied.note: Checked against the Government Printer edition -- the Act as published as a supplement to Part II of the Gazette of 4 October 2002, certified the same day -- which the Survey Department publishes as a PDF with a text layer. quality_flags.detail: The tree is parsed from LankaLaw, a private republisher. A Government Printer edition of this Act exists, has a text layer, and was used to check the parse -- but the text below is still LankaLaw's transcription, and the two differ in wording throughout.

Section 10's marginal note, "Preparation of Cadastral plans and maps.", was printed inside the body of subsection (1). It is corrected into the heading and left in raw_text and text, where it still interrupts the sentence.

Sections 10 (2), 25 (1) and 25 (2) each open a lettered pair and the source marks up only the (b) limb, so (a) is carried inside the subsection's own text rather than as a paragraph node. Not synthesised: inventing the container would change the tree on inference alone. Both editions print (a) and (b).

Section 66 defines 15 terms in the Government Printer edition. This tree types 11. "Cadastral survey" is untyped because the parsed edition drops its opening quotation mark, and "Department" because a stray full stop is printed before its opening quote; both are held as closing_text nodes beside the definitions and carry their full wording. Section 39 requires the qualifications specified in the Schedule, and the parsed page carries no Schedule. The body under `schedules` was read off the Government Printer edition and is marked as such; it is not part of the parse.

No amending Act is recorded for this Act in this corpus and the parsed page carries no amendment chain in its header. That is the absence of a finding, not a finding of no amendments: nothing here has checked the Gazette.
